---
title: "2026-05-26"
output: html_document
date: "2026-05-25"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyplots)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggtext)
library(tidyr)

#download TidyTuesday data
tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2026-05-26')

energy_cleaned <- tuesdata$energy_cleaned

```

``` {r Sample Plot}
# framing: of 3 windy countries, which one has consumed the most wind power?
# A quick Google search suggested Denmark, Ireland, and Norway
target_countries <- c("Denmark", "Ireland", "Norway")
the_windies <- energy_cleaned |>
filter(country_name %in% target_countries) |>
select(
country_name,
yr,
wind_energy_consumption_tfec_pct
)
the_windies <- the_windies |>
mutate(yr = as.numeric(yr))

# creating the plot
sample_plot <- the_windies |>
tidyplot(x = yr, y = wind_energy_consumption_tfec_pct, color = country_name, fill = country_name) |>
add(
ggplot2::geom_area(position = "identity")
) |>
adjust_x_axis_title("Year") |>
adjust_y_axis_title("Wind energy consumption (% in TFEC)") |>
add_title("Wind Power Consumed by Population and Industry (%)") |>
add_caption("Denmark and Ireland maintained an upward trend upto 2010, but
Norway's consumption **levels out from 2007**."
) |>
adjust_size(width = 140, height = 120) |>
theme_tidyplot() +
theme(
plot.title = element_text(family = "roboto",size = 16, face = "bold", vjust = 10, margin = margin(t = 10)),
axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, margin = margin(r = 18)),
axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, margin = margin(t = 18)),
axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 11),
axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 11),
plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 12, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 20), lineheight = 1.5),
legend.position = "top",
legend.title = element_blank(),
legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
) +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("#009e73", "#56b4e9", "#d55e00")) +
scale_color_manual(values = c("#009e73", "#56b4e9", "#d55e00"))

# saving the plot image
ggsave(
"sample_plot.png",
sample_plot,
width = 10,
height = 8,
limitsize = FALSE
)
```

```{r Filter to Canada}
cdn_energy <- energy_cleaned %>%
    filter(country_code == "CAN")

colnames(cdn_energy)
```

```{r}
#make energy intensity by sector into long format
intensity_long <- cdn_energy %>%
  select(
    yr,
    Agricultural = energy_intensity_agricultural_sector_megajoules_per_usd_2005,
    Industrial   = energy_intensity_industrial_sector_megajoules_per_usd_2005,
    Other        = energy_intensity_other_sectors_megajoules_per_usd_2005
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Agricultural, Industrial, Other),
    names_to = "Sector",
    values_to = "Energy_Intensity"
  )

#make grouped bar plot 
ggplot(intensity_long, aes(x = as.factor(yr), y = Energy_Intensity, fill = Sector, group = Sector)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_line(aes(y = Energy_Intensity, color = Sector, group = Sector), 
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), size = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Energy Intensity by Sector (Canada) with Trend Lines",
    x = "Year",
    y = "MJ per USD (2005 PPP)",
    fill = "Sector",
    color = "Trend"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
#make it so graph only shows labels for every 5 years
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = unique(intensity_long$yr)[seq(1, length(unique(intensity_long$yr)), 5)]) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
